🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Wednesday, 4 November 2026

1. 🏛️ Home Secretary sets out response to earned settlement consultation
The Home Secretary made a statement to Parliament on the government's response to the earned settlement consultation.

2. 💷 Government says new EU deal could add up to £5.1bn a year to economy
The government has estimated that a deal with the EU could add up to £5.1 billion a year to the economy.

3. 🏠 Housing market unlikely to recover until 2028, says Savills
The property firm expects house prices to fall by 1.5% next year, after drifting lower for the rest of 2026.

4. 🔥 Palace of Westminster at risk of Notre Dame-style fire, committee warns
A parliamentary committee said the building risks a Notre Dame-style fire or similar catastrophe if MPs do not tackle refurbishment funding.

5. 📚 Ukrainian GCSE to be offered to students in three UK nations from 2028
Students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be able to take a Ukrainian GCSE from 2028 as part of government plans.

6. 🩺 Multi-cancer blood tests are coming to some GP surgeries soon
The tests aim to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner.

7. 🖥️ UK fridges hacked in cyberattack that spoiled millions of euros of food
The attack caused millions of euros worth of fresh and frozen food to be spoiled.

8. 👑 King Charles says slavery has made him determined to address past wrongs
Speaking in Antigua, the King did not explicitly back reparations.

Sources: Free Movement, The Independent, Guardian, Sky News, BBC. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Lauren Hurley / No 10 Downing Street / OGL 3, Wikimedia Commons; White House / Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

items.title: Home Secretary sets out response to earned settlement consultation
items.body: The Home Secretary made a statement to Parliament on the government's response to the earned settlement consultation. The Home Office has published its full response to the 'A Fairer Pathway to Settlement' consultation.

items.title: Government says new EU deal could add up to £5.1bn a year to economy
items.body: The government has estimated that a deal with the EU could add up to £5.1 billion a year to the economy. The story looks at which Brexit laws could be scrapped under a new agreement.

items.title: Housing market unlikely to recover until 2028, says Savills
items.body: The property firm expects house prices to fall by 1.5% next year, after drifting lower for the rest of 2026. It says higher mortgage rates linked to the war in the Middle East are deterring buyers.

items.title: Palace of Westminster at risk of Notre Dame-style fire, committee warns
items.body: A parliamentary committee said the building risks a Notre Dame-style fire or similar catastrophe if MPs do not tackle refurbishment funding. Maintenance costs could soon reach £2m a week, including 24-hour patrols.

items.title: King Charles says slavery has made him determined to address past wrongs
items.body: Speaking in Antigua, the King did not explicitly back reparations. Caribbean leaders and campaigners have intensified demands for an apology and reparations from Britain.
